text: Cent #478.
A penny struck in 1963, at Philadelphia.
Under the word TRUST, the copper has darkened.
That is called significant obsidian.
At his collar, and around
the word GOD, pale, dry films.
Notable desert.
Across LIBERTY and down the shoulder,
small dark particles lie scattered.
A contamination called Speckles.
Compare Cent #3525,
also from 1963, whose only trait is Lustrous.
The same design, the same year, a different surface.
None of these names came with the Cents.
Traits named by the community.
In the words of Steven Reiss,
in his article "Materiality and Signification":
"Unlike most NFT projects,
CENTS offered no preset rarity
traits beyond mint year and mint mark.
The community therefore began
naming the spontaneous variations."
A Trait Council of collectors spent
about two years naming, defining and voting.
Speckles is one of twelve kinds
of contamination they recognised.
95 Cents carry it.
Four of them are from 1963.
Value made by consensus.
In the words of Martin Lehnen,
in his essay "CENTS as an artistic expression
of Bitcoin's core ideas": "Just as the project
removes the authority of the state in determining
a penny's worth, it also removes the authority
of a single artist or institution
in defining its significance."
